title: Sol architecture: minimal authoritative historical workflow inventory
description: Design the smallest read-only Gas City core capability that can answer whether an exact workflow launch existed and reached terminal state across live and historical/deleted workflow records. This is the external prerequisite identified by gp-804tx.54.15. Search current code and git history before proposing anything. Reuse the existing beads/event/coordination substrate; do not add a new primitive or embed PR-intake policy in core. The output must attest query scope, retention coverage, completeness, canonical digest, observation time, exact workflow identity, lifecycle, and terminal time. If the retained substrate cannot prove historical completeness for the August 21 launches, say so and keep reconciliation checkpoint-only.
design: Apply the Gas City Primitive Test and upstream-alignment rules. Prefer a narrow domain read model plus CLI projection; HTTP/OpenAPI only if an existing object-model path requires it. The query is generic workflow execution history, filtered by city/rig/source identity, not a gascity-packs-specific endpoint. It is read-only, bounded, deterministic, and fail-closed. Deleted/GC records may count only when the existing durable substrate guarantees retention from the requested launch time. No graph/convoy inference, resurrection, mutation, purge, or synthesized launch identity.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture identifies the authoritative existing substrate and proves its retention/completeness semantics or explicitly reports that proof is impossible. Closed request/response schemas cover city, rig, source store, namespace, observation/retention bounds, exact workflow/source/launch identity, lifecycle, terminal_at, canonical result digest, and completeness. No hardcoded role or repository policy enters Go. CLI/API ownership and exact minimal files/tests are specified; history archaeology is documented. Failure/outage/retention gaps return incomplete, never a false complete empty result. The design states whether it can reconcile the four August 21 launches. No code, ledger cleanup, workflow execution, or GitHub mutation occurs.
notes: ARCHITECTURE RESULT (2026-08-23): existing Gas City beads/events substrate cannot truthfully attest complete retained all-history workflow inventory. Aug-21 archives positively associate gp-c5i10, gp-jshkf, gp-oxgcw, and gp-wzdgf with four workflow roots, but events are best-effort/retention-prunable, live-root queries exclude closed/deleted records, and no record binds complete launch nonce/attempt/source-version identity plus lifecycle/terminal_at. This prerequisite therefore yields CHECKPOINT_UNCERTAIN for all four; no claim/source/capacity/terminal mutation is authorized. A future capability must be a generic core launch-history read model with exact scope, retention coverage, completeness, digest, identity, lifecycle, and terminal_at—not workflows-local inference.
close_reason: Architecture completed: current substrate cannot supply authoritative historical inventory

title: Sol architecture delta: production city-source CAS boundary
description: Resolve the newly proven production boundary gap for gp-804tx.54.4. The approved gp-804tx.53 design requires guarded expected-identity/source-version/operation-id CAS before sling, but deployed gc 1.4.1 d551aa9066 with bd 1.2.1 c7d6033c1 exposes no CLI expected-metadata/operation-id flags. Inspect existing Beads row-version and metadata-CAS capabilities, including POST /v0/beads/issues/{id}:casMetadata, and choose the smallest production-usable city-qualified protocol. Specify canonical authority record, operation idempotency, source projection repair, ambiguous outcome retention, attestation/readback, crash boundaries, and deployment/runtime requirements. Keep the order disabled; no live source or GitHub mutation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exact supported production API/command and ownership repo are identified from deployed artifacts.
- One atomic CAS authority record binds source ID, external ref, head SHA, attempt, source version, claim fence/nonce, launch ID, operation ID, state, and successor version.
- Retry, mismatch, outage, crash-before/after-CAS, projection lag, and ambiguous-response semantics fail closed and retain capacity where required.
- Formula, sweep, reconciliation, and selector consumers are specified; raw unguarded source writes are forbidden.
- Sol records APPROVE_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION or BLOCK; BLOCK leaves this decision bead open.
notes:
SOL ARCHITECTURE VERDICT 2026-08-21 — APPROVE_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION.\n\nProduction primitive: deployed gc 1.4.1 supports exact-local-store atomic single-key CAS:\ngc --city <absolute-maintainer-city> beads metadata-cas <source-id> --store-ref=rig:gascity-packs --key=pr_intake.authority --expected=<canonical-old> --next=<canonical-new> --json\nNo scan, fallback, or remote store is permitted. The closed response schema v1 must be parsed strictly; swapped/already_next/conflict are classified zero-exit outcomes, while validation/capability/transport/readback failures are nonzero and fail closed.\n\nAuthority is one compact, sorted-key canonical JSON string at pr_intake.authority, schema v1, with exactly: schema_version, source_bead_id, external_ref, pr_head_sha (lowercase 40hex), attempt, claim_kind, claim_nonce, launch_id, operation_id, state, source_version_before, source_version_after (= before + 1). Each transition compares the exact prior canonical string (empty only at initial acquisition) and supplies the exact successor. Local WAL/intent and reservation precede CAS.\n\nswapped or already_next succeeds only after exact same-store bd show --json readback equals desired authority. conflict is no-write/stale-or-foreign unless readback equals desired (idempotent race). Same operation_id with divergent authority is SOURCE_VERSION_CONFLICT. Nonzero, invalid response, or failed readback is uncertain: retain claim/capacity, never sling, never release, and never blind-retry. Reconciliation may retry the identical CAS only when readback is exactly expected; exact desired attests commit; all other values hold for reconciliation.\n\npr_intake.authority is sole mutable authority. Legacy sibling pr_intake.* fields may be stable indexing projections but never authorize work; divergence fails closed. Replace raw authoritative bd update paths in sweep/formula/reconciliation; formula validates the sweep handoff and never acquires. Sequence: durable local intent/reservation -> authority CAS/readback -> sling -> strict graph/source readback -> formula validation. Keep pr-intake-sweep disabled and gp-804tx.54.4 open through implementation and council. No live source or GitHub mutation occurred.
SOL ARCHITECTURE DELTA 2026-08-21 — APPROVE_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION

Decision boundary

The production blocker is resolved by the already-deployed Gas City command, not by a new Beads or Gas City feature:

  gc --city <absolute-city> beads metadata-cas <source-bead-id> --store-ref=rig:gascity-packs --key=pr_intake.authority --expected=<canonical-old> --next=<canonical-new> --json

Verified against deployed gc 1.4.1. The command selects one exact local store, never scans, follows a fallback, or operates remotely. Its closed JSON schema v1 returns ok=true plus the exact bead_id, canonical store_ref, key, and one zero-exit outcome: swapped, already_next, or conflict. Validation, capability, transport, close, and required readback failures are nonzero. No Beads CLI, Gas City, or deployment work is required; gp-804tx.54.12 is a workflows adapter/protocol change.

Canonical authority record

pr_intake.authority is the sole mutable PR-intake authority. Its value is a canonical compact JSON string, UTF-8, keys sorted lexicographically, no insignificant whitespace, integer numbers encoded canonically, and exactly these fields:

  schema_version: 1
  source_bead_id: gp-...
  external_ref: gh:gastownhall/gascity-packs#<number>
  pr_head_sha: 40 lowercase hex
  attempt: integer >= 1
  claim_kind: investigation | review-promotion
  claim_nonce: nonempty fence token
  launch_id: deterministic launch identity
  operation_id: deterministic transition identity
  state: a closed PR-intake state
  source_version_before: integer >= 0
  source_version_after: source_version_before + 1

The CLI compares strings, so byte-identical canonical encoding is a correctness requirement. For a transition from version N to N+1, expected is the exact previously read and validated authority string whose source_version_after is N; next has source_version_before=N and source_version_after=N+1. Initial acquisition alone uses --expected= for an absent/empty authority key and writes the complete version 0→1 claimed record. All identity, claim, launch, operation, state, and version fields advance in the same single-key atomic CAS.

Transition and classification protocol

- Before CAS: validate exact source/store/PR/head/attempt/fence identity; persist local ClaimStore reservation plus launch/source intent in the WAL. No sling is permitted yet.
- swapped: candidate commit. Strictly re-read the same bead through the same city/rig boundary and require pr_intake.authority to equal the exact desired canonical string before attesting success.
- already_next: idempotent candidate. Apply the same exact readback rule; only equality with desired is success.
- conflict: definitive no-write by this attempt. Re-read. Exact desired means an idempotent concurrent/replayed success; the same operation_id with any divergent record is SOURCE_VERSION_CONFLICT; any other record is stale/foreign ownership and remains held for reconciliation.
- Nonzero exit, invalid JSON/schema/identity, missing authority, or failed readback: outcome is uncertain. Retain the claim, intent, and capacity; do not sling, release, overwrite, or blindly retry.
- Reconciliation after uncertainty: exact desired authority attests the commit; exact expected authority permits replay of the identical expected/next CAS while the same valid claim is retained; every other value remains conflict/uncertain and requires reconciliation. Never infer success from CLI exit alone.

Idempotency and conflict rules

operation_id is deterministic for source bead, external ref, head, attempt, claim kind, transition, source version, launch identity, and desired semantic payload. A replay is successful only when the entire desired authority record matches. Reuse of an operation_id with a different canonical record is SOURCE_VERSION_CONFLICT. A stale head, attempt, nonce/fence, launch, source version, or source bead always writes nothing and fails closed. There is no unguarded fallback.

Projection policy

Immutable/index fields such as pr_intake.external_ref, pr_intake.pr_head_sha, and pr_intake.attempt may temporarily remain for inventory compatibility, but consumers derive mutable state, version, fence, launch, and operation identity only from pr_intake.authority. Legacy pr_intake.state, pr_intake.source_version, pr_intake.publication_operation_id, outcome, and failure keys cannot authorize work and must no longer be mutated as transition authority. If any retained projection disagrees with the parsed authority record, hold work and repair the projection only through a separately guarded/reconciled path; never let last-write-wins projection repair advance authority.

Crash and outage boundaries

- Crash before local intent/reservation: no source write and no capacity consumed.
- Crash after local intent/reservation but before CAS: capacity remains held; reconciliation may replay the identical CAS.
- Crash after CAS but before attestation: capacity remains held; exact desired same-store readback attests commit.
- Crash after attestation but before sling: resume from durable attestation; do not acquire or CAS again except an exact idempotent replay check.
- Crash/timeout during sling or before strict graph/source readback: state is uncertain and capacity remains held; never re-sling blindly.
- CAS/store/readback outage or malformed source authority: fail closed and retain capacity.

Required workflows changes in gp-804tx.54.12

1. Adapt CitySourceAdapter to invoke gc beads metadata-cas with the fixed rig:gascity-packs store ref, pr_intake.authority key, canonical expected/next strings, --json, closed schema validation, and strict same-store bd show readback.
2. Replace all authoritative raw gc ... bd update mutations in the sweep, formula setup/snapshot/failure/finalization paths, and reconciliation helpers. Add a static/graph test that rejects such raw authority writes.
3. Make SourceRecord and all selector/formula/reconciliation consumers parse and validate the authority record. Formula validates the handed-off claim and never acquires a second claim.
4. Preserve sequencing: local WAL and capacity reservation → source authority CAS and exact attestation → sling → strict sling/graph/source readback → formula fanout.
5. Keep ClaimStore/WAL as cross-store intent and capacity authority. A source/CAS outage, ambiguous response, projection divergence, unresolved launch, or partial sling retains capacity.
6. Preserve the four accidental-launch reconciliation fixtures as no-write evidence and add tests for canonicalization, first acquisition, swap, already_next replay, conflict, divergent operation replay, stale identity/head/attempt/version/fence, crashes around CAS/attestation/sling, outage/readback failure, projection divergence, and exactly-one reservation end to end.

Release posture

This approval releases Terra to gp-804tx.54.12. It does not approve gp-804tx.54.4, the live pilot, source reconciliation, GitHub mutation, or order enablement. Keep pr-intake-sweep enabled=false until implementation, focused tests, preserved no-write reconciliation, and fresh contract/safety/operations Sol councils all pass.
close_reason: Sol APPROVE_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION: deployed exact-store metadata-cas and canonical single-key authority protocol fully specified; Terra may implement while order remains disabled.

title: issue-374 W2: D1+D2 formula guard insertion and D3 inference-gate repin (atomic)
description:
Atomic implementation work item for issue 374 (`mol-refinery-patrol` rebase-skip guard).
Implements design sections **D1**, **D2** and **D3** in ONE commit.

Traces: AC-374-01, AC-374-02, AC-374-03, AC-374-05, AC-374-06, AC-374-07.

## Atomicity constraint (AC-374-07)

The formula change and the inference-gate repin land together. **Never formula without
gate.** Splitting this item is a contract violation.

## D1 — formula insertion (`gastown/formulas/mol-refinery-patrol.toml`, step `rebase`)

Pure INSERTION into the step's fenced block, between the halt's closing `fi` at base
`:293` and base `:294`. Everything from `:248` through `:293` stays byte-identical.
Order: prune-fetch -> halt -> guard-fetch -> probe -> case.

The inserted block is specified verbatim in approved-design.md D1. Load-bearing
properties:

- Explicit dual-refspec force-fetch of exactly the two decision refs, **exit checked**,
  failing closed (echo + `gc runtime drain-ack` + `exit 1`; no probe, no checkout, no
  rebase, zero bead mutation). Refspecs deliberately **unbraced** (`$BRANCH`/`$TARGET`) —
  string-distinct from the braced merge-push `:790` so the gate pin witnesses this site
  uniquely. Keep the fence comment recording that intent.
- The guard fetch MUST follow the halt: explicit-fetching a missing `$TARGET` exits 128
  and would swallow `target_branch_missing` into a generic STOP, bypassing the halt's
  park + escalation + wisp-pour.
- Probe `git merge-base --is-ancestor "origin/$TARGET" "origin/$BRANCH"` (target->source,
  quoted) — the string-reverse of merge-push `:795`, which is untouched.
- Capture by bare invocation with `ANCESTOR_RC=$?` on the NEXT line. Never `if !`
  (negation clobbers the status); never a zsh reserved name (`status` is read-only).
- Three-way `case`: rc 0 = skip (exit-checked `git checkout -b temp origin/$BRANCH`, then
  the `SKIP-REBASE:` echo); rc 1 = the preserved, unquoted, byte-identical
  `git rebase origin/$TARGET` preceded by today's exact bare checkout; any other rc =
  STOP, never read as "not an ancestor", never routed into the conflict-rejection path.
- STOP arms carry NO `rejection_reason`, no delete/reopen-source, no polecat reroute, no
  `gc bd update` of any kind.

## D2 — step-prose amendments (same step, nothing removed)

1. Insert before base `:298` the SKIP outcome paragraph (skip is a first-class success;
   do not abort, amend, reset, or re-run a rebase on it).
2. Amend the conflict preamble base `:300-:301` to the "and only then" wording.
3. Append one sentence to the step's intro rationale (base `:235-:246`).

Exact wording is normative in approved-design.md D2. Prose spells the token backticked
and colon-free (`SKIP-REBASE`) — preserve that convention.

## D3 — inference-gate repin (`scripts/gascity_pack_inference_gate.py`)

`GASTOWN_BUILD_WORKFLOW_CONTRACTS["mol-refinery-patrol"]` command dict (base `:122`).
Containment is whole-file, at-least-once, deletion-only (`fragment not in text` over
`formulas/<formula>.toml` alone).

At fix time **enumerate every `mol-refinery-patrol` site by grep and re-derive line
numbers; never assert a count** (at base: command dict `:122`, prose dict `:91`, and the
`setup_formulas` registry entry `:790`, which needs no change).

- Preserved pin that keeps matching: `git rebase origin/$TARGET`.
- Five added fragments, each satisfiable only by the new block:
  1. `git fetch origin "+refs/heads/$BRANCH:refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH"`
  2. `git merge-base --is-ancestor "origin/$TARGET" "origin/$BRANCH"`
  3. `ANCESTOR_RC=$?`
  4. `cannot evaluate rebase ancestry. STOP. Do not mutate bead state.`

title: issue-374 W1: regression test test_mol_refinery_patrol_rebase_guard.sh (D4, test-first)
description:
Test-first work item for issue 374 (`mol-refinery-patrol` rebase-skip guard).
Implements design section **D4** and builds the red-control capability.

Traces: AC-374-04 (primary), AC-374-01, AC-374-02, AC-374-03, AC-374-05, AC-374-06.

## Scope

Create `gastown/tests/test_mol_refinery_patrol_rebase_guard.sh` (CI auto-discovers
`gastown/tests/test_*.sh`). Witness-suite conventions: `#!/usr/bin/env bash`,
`set -euo pipefail` in the harness, `mktemp -d` + `trap` cleanup, `fail()` helper,
awk `lift_block`.

- **Lift, never transcribe.** Lift the step's fenced bash block whole from the shipped
  TOML using sentinel `git checkout -b temp origin/$BRANCH` (present in BOTH the
  unguarded and guarded formula, so reds are behavioral, not lift errors; it appears
  twice in the guarded text within the one lifted fence — use sentinel-indexed
  extraction). Execute as one unit. Mechanical substitutions only
  (`{{target_branch}}`->`main`, `{{rig_name}}`->`testrig`, `{{binding_prefix}}`->``,
  `<bead>`-style ids->`TESTBEAD`), then `bash -n`.
- **Execution wrapper:** `set +eu` subshell sourcing under plain `bash`; stdout and rc
  captured per leg.
- **Hermetic fixtures:** bare `origin.git` + consumer clone per leg; `git config
  user.name/email` in every committing repo; `HOME`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` redirected into
  the tmpdir and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` set (git 2.43 local vs 2.52 CI identity
  divergence; a host `/etc/gitconfig` must not leak). Fixture shapes: **EX-1**
  already-based/conflicting, **EX-2** already-based/clean, **EX-3a** diverged/clean,
  **EX-3b** diverged/conflicting.
- **Version-stable assertions:** assert the `SKIP-REBASE:` prefix and non-zero fetch rc,
  never short-SHA length or an undocumented git exit code. Exactly TWO scoped carve-outs:
  leg 6's `errored (status 128)` (the shim's own deterministic exit) and leg 3's rc 1
  (git's empirically stable rebase-conflict code; measured on git 2.43 — re-confirm on the
  CI git at fix time). Leg 5 stays `rc != 0` with 128 recorded in a comment as observation
  only; it must never harden into a third exact-code carve-out.
- **Red-control mechanism (build the capability here):** resolve the formula path
  witness-style with an env override
  `FORMULA="${REBASE_GUARD_FORMULA:-$ROOT/gastown/formulas/mol-refinery-patrol.toml}"`
  so the identical test file can be aimed at another tree.
- **Harness preflight:** `command -v jq >/dev/null || fail "jq required (halt leg)"`.
  The halt's wisp-pour pipes through real `jq` unconditionally (base `:273`), so the suite
  carries a hard `jq` dependency. Do NOT shadow `jq` in the stub PATH — the pour-id
  extraction must genuinely parse the stub's JSON answer.
- **`gc` stub:** PATH shim logging every invocation to `$GC_LOG` (the bead-mutation
  oracle); serves `bd show`/`bd list` canned JSON; answers wisp-pour with
  `{"new_epic_id":...}`; no-ops the rest; drain-ack inert but logged. Env
  `BRANCH`/`TARGET`/`WORK` and `GC_BEAD_ID` supplied.

## Legs (nine)

1. Skip preserves topology (EX-1, EX-2).
1b. Stranded `temp` fails closed at the skip-arm checkout.
2. Diverged clean rebases as today (EX-3a).
3. Diverged conflicting keeps the conflict path (EX-3b); cleanup `git rebase --abort`.
4. Fetch failure stops before the probe (stale-ref trap; then restore + re-run).
5. Missing source branch.
6. Probe error fails closed (passthrough git shim intercepting ONLY `merge-base` -> 128,
   real git resolved to an absolute path first; shim prepended to PATH only inside the
   lifted-fence execution subshell — fixture setup and assertions run with real git).
7. Structural backstop + ordering (static, raw fence text).
8. Halt composition: delete `main` on the bare origin; assert the park shape in `$GC_LOG`.

Leg specifications are normative in approved-design.md D4 — implement them as written
there, including every per-leg assertion and each documented *Red on base* expectation.

## Verification (both halves required)

- Static: leg 7's three count assertions — probe line exactly once; lift sentinel
  `git checkout -b temp origin/$BRANCH` exactly twice; the substring
  `cannot evaluate rebase ancestry` exactly twice. Leg 7 also asserts the lifted block
  contains both explicit refspecs, `ANCESTOR_RC=$?`, and the per-arm STOP literals
  `tracking refs failed`, `errored (status `, and `cannot materialize temp at origin/`,
  plus the full ordering chain and `bash -n`.
- Behavioral: legs 1, 1b, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 against the guarded tree.
- This item is complete only when both halves exist; a leg that drops its static or its
  behavioral half is incomplete.

Do not reword any pinned literal above — the harness pins and red controls depend on the
exact strings.

title: witness orphan salvage publishes branches without consulting the push gate
description:
The polecat push gate in `mol-polecat-work` (`submit-and-exit`) fails closed: a
bead whose prose asserts a no-push rail with no `auto_push` metadata halts at
branch-ready and escalates instead of pushing. That property holds ONLY on the
polecat's own submit-and-exit path.

`mol-witness-patrol`'s orphan salvage (Cases C and D, `recover-orphaned-beads`)
runs `git push origin HEAD` unconditionally. It does not probe
`metadata.auto_push` and does not scan the bead's prose. So a polecat that DIES
mid-work on a bead that must not reach the remote is recovered by salvage and
its branch is published anyway -- the exact customer-estate failure the gate
exists to prevent, one path over.

The mayor prompt already concedes this in prose ("even it is not enforced on
that path") but referenced no tracking bead, so the concession had nowhere to
land. Raised as a major finding by two independent reviewers in the post-merge
review of PR #273 (range 5bffaf7..ef28498); the review's bounded share was the
two-way cross-reference, filed here as the real fix.

Pre-existing: `mol-witness-patrol.toml` is untouched by #273. This is not a
regression introduced there.
design:
Teach salvage Cases C and D to consult the recorded decision before publishing.

Minimum viable shape, mirroring the gate's own precedence:

1. Read the bead with the SAME normalising probe the gate uses (object / null /
   JSON-string metadata all decode; the key and the value are both case-folded;
   the value vocabulary is closed: false|no|0 -> false, true|yes|1 -> true).
   The probe is duplicated prose today -- consider lifting it into one shared
   snippet both formulas render, since it has already drifted once between the
   gate and the mayor's read-back recipe.
2. `auto_push=false` (explicit opt-out) -> do NOT push. Commit the work, leave
   the branch local, record `branch` and `branch_ready=true`, and mail the
   witness/mayor the way the gate's halts do. The work is still salvaged; only
   the publish is withheld.
3. `auto_push=true` -> push, as today.
4. Absent / unreadable -> the open question. The gate halts here, but salvage
   runs on a bead whose agent is already gone, so a halt strands the work
   rather than costing a round trip. Options: halt and escalate (consistent
   with the gate, strictly safer), or push and mail loudly (preserves today's
   recovery behaviour). Decide deliberately and record the reasoning next to
   the code, as the gate does.

This changes witness behaviour on a path PR #273 does not touch, so it wants
its own review with its own test evidence -- the reason it is not folded into
#273's post-merge remediation.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: an executed test, in the style of
`gastown/tests/test_polecat_push_gate.sh`, that lifts the salvage recipe out of
the SHIPPED `mol-witness-patrol.toml` step and runs it against stubbed `gc`
and `git`, pinning at minimum:
- a bead with `metadata.auto_push=false` and unpushed commits: work is
  committed, `PUSH` never happens, the branch is recorded;
- the same bead with `auto_push=true`: `PUSH` happens (so the guard cannot be
  satisfied by never pushing);
- whichever absent/unreadable behaviour is chosen, pinned in both directions;
- the case-variant key (`AUTO_PUSH`) and the string-shaped metadata payload,
  since both defeated the gate's probe before it was normalised.
Plus: the mayor prompt's concession and the witness prompt/formula
cross-references are updated to describe the enforced behaviour rather than
pointing here.

error-routing residual that the design accepts but requires to be TRACKED, not merely
narrated in committed prose.

## Scope

File the residual-precision-(b) follow-up **family** as a tracked work item and link it
from the PR body. The design is explicit: "committed prose alone is not the tracking."

The family is ONE item with two members sharing the same assigned head-of-line class:

1. **Deleted-`$BRANCH` park mirror.** A permanently-deleted `$BRANCH` becomes an
   assigned, never-healing STOP — a head-of-line risk by the missing-`$TARGET` halt's own
   rationale. Parking it would require bead mutation on an error path, which this
   contract forbids here; hence the mirror of the `$TARGET` halt is deferred, not
   implemented.
2. **Repeated stranded-`temp` checkout-STOP.** A checkout-STOP hit repeatedly on the same
   stranded `temp` is operationally the same assigned head-of-line class. Clearing the
   stale branch itself remains a human/merge-push-side concern; the pre-existing
   stranded-`temp` hazard at merge-push STOPs (`:826-:829`, `:838-:841`) is out of scope
   and must NOT be "fixed" in this change.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

Do not widen the STOP semantics, do not add bead mutation to any error path, and do not
modify merge-push. This item files tracking; it does not implement either mirror.

title: gastown: sibling patrols never claim their wisps, and prompt/formula disagree on ending the turn (post-merge #261 follow-up)
description:
Carried forward from the **post-merge** review of PR #261 (root
`gcg-5436965277323002`, attempt 1), applied in follow-up PR #420. Non-gating for
#420; filed so the findings are not lost in a PR body. Sibling of `mc-x80bo`,
which covers the deacon's `drain-ack` + `exit 1` instance specifically.

## Finding 1 — the never-claimed-wisp lifecycle is pack-wide, not boot-only

PR #420 fixes boot: startup now runs `gc bd update "$WISP" --status=in_progress`
after pour+assign, so the queries that filter on `in_progress` can actually
resolve. The review (F1(f)) allowed that remedy to stay boot-scoped provided the
deacon-observation query was widened instead, which #420 does. The underlying
shape is still present in every sibling patrol.

Measured on `gastown/formulas/` at `e013296` (`gc bd update … --status=in_progress`
occurrences vs `--status=in_progress` reads):

| formula | reads `in_progress` | sets `in_progress` |
|---|---|---|
| `mol-deacon-patrol.toml` | 2 | **0** |
| `mol-refinery-patrol.toml` | 5 | **0** |
| `mol-witness-patrol.toml` | 2 | **0** |
| `mol-boot-patrol.toml` (after #420) | 2 | 1 |

Nothing else sets it: `gc` exports `GC_BEAD_ID` only into ralph check scripts,
and these patrols have no hook-claim block. So for each of the three, the same
consequences boot had apply — the burn arm is unreachable, the "could not
resolve current wisp" diagnostic prints on healthy cycles, restart-resume cannot
happen, and each cycle re-pours and leans on the surplus burn.

The refinery is the one to look at first: 5 reads is the widest exposure.

Remedy: apply boot's shape per agent — claim after pour+assign, and reuse an
already-assigned `open` wisp before pouring. Do this per-agent rather than as one
sweep; each patrol's reconcile block differs and the deacon's is entangled with
`mc-x80bo`.

## Finding 2 — prompt and formula disagree about ending the turn

`drain-ack` mentions at `e013296`:

| agent | prompt | formula |
|---|---|---|
| witness | 1 | **0** |
| refinery | **0** | 41 |
| deacon | 0 | 3 |

The refinery's formula is saturated with `drain-ack` while its prompt never
mentions it; the witness is the mirror image. An agent reading only its prompt
and an agent reading only its formula get different end-turn contracts, which is
the exact confusion that produced #261's original hot loop. Reconcile each pair
so the end-turn contract is stated once and consistently.

## Explicitly not in scope

The deacon's two `$GC_ALIAS` sites. Gemini's orphan premise there was **refuted**
during the #261 review — `GC_ALIAS` is non-empty for named sessions, so
propagating `$GC_AGENT` would be a no-op. Do not file it as an "orphan fix".

title: mol-refinery-patrol: already-merged gate is rebase-blind (ancestry-only, no patch-id or content tier)
description:
The `already-merged` classification in `mol-refinery-patrol` still decides
"has this branch landed?" with a bare ancestry test, so a branch that landed by
rebase or squash is misclassified as unlanded.

Site: `gastown/formulas/mol-refinery-patrol.toml:710` --
`git merge-base --is-ancestor "origin/$BRANCH" "origin/$TARGET"`. The
`ANCESTOR_STATUS` case handling is careful about errors (status `*` STOPs) and
about zero-commit branches (status `0` re-checks `fork_sha..origin/$BRANCH`),
but status `1` is `: ;` -- a plain fall-through to the normal merge-candidate
path. A rebased or squashed landing is not an ancestor of the target, so it
takes that fall-through and gets routed as if it never landed: halted as a
false completion, or re-merged.

This is the same defect class fixed on the witness side by
gastownhall/gascity-packs#320 (fixes #286), which replaced the witness's
ancestry-only check with tiered detection: ancestry, then patch-id
(`git cherry`), then a content diff scoped to the branch's own changed files,
with every uncertain outcome falling through to "not merged". #320 also
establishes in its own rationale that rebase/squash landing is the normal case
here, not an edge case. The witness fix deliberately did not touch the refinery
so the PR stayed one file; the codex review of #320 raised the surviving
sibling site, and the quality scorecard carried it as required tracking item
F11 rather than as a code change in #320.

Suggested fix: port the tiered detection from
`gastown/formulas/mol-witness-patrol.toml` (Step 3c of `recover-orphaned-beads`)
into the refinery's status-`1` arm -- patch-id tier first, then the
changed-files content diff, preserving the existing `fork_sha` / `REAL_COMMITS`
zero-commit discriminator and the fail-closed default of "not merged". Reuse
the same NUL-safe changed-file expansion.

Related but distinct: gp-z6saa (Issue #374) covers the refinery's *rebase* step
skipping the rebase when the target is already an ancestor of a merge-heavy
source. That is the rebase leg; this bead is the already-merged classification
leg.

Provenance: raised in the PR #320 adopt-pr review loop (codex-review finding
"The same ancestry-only blind spot this PR fixes remains live in the refinery's
already-merged classification"; quality-scorecard Required Changes F11).

title: Scope bead reads to the owning store in the three sibling approval gates
description:
PR #350 added owning-store scoping (resolve_show_scope) to gascity/assets/scripts/checks/build-artifact-valid.sh only. Three sibling gates still read beads from the ambient store and hit the same wrong-store failure mode:

- gascity/assets/scripts/checks/design-review-approved.sh:46 (BEAD_JSON)
- gascity/assets/scripts/checks/gap-analysis-approved.sh:59 (ROOT_JSON)
- gascity/assets/scripts/checks/implementation-review-approved.sh:59,66 (ROOT_JSON, PARENT_JSON)

Deliberately left out of PR #350's apply-fixes iteration: the review scored this non-gating (quality-scorecard.md F5) and touching three production approval gates in a review-fix commit expands blast radius well past the reviewed change. Do it as its own change with its own review.

Approach: hoist resolve_show_scope / scope_from_store_ref / show_bead_with_retry out of build-artifact-valid.sh into a sourced helper beside the checks, then adopt it in all four gates. Note the three siblings swallow read failures with '2>/dev/null || true' and treat an unreadable bead as 'not approved', so scoping them changes gate outcomes and needs its own test coverage per gate.

title: witness patrol: sweep for no-tier beads (open + unassigned + gc.routed_to empty)
description:
The Gas Town lifecycle migration (PR #380) replaced atomic
`gc bd update --status=... --assignee=""` writes with dedicated verbs, which
splits "release the bead and record why" into two commands. Every such site is
now ordered record-first so a crash lands on in_progress + assigned (lease
expiry / `bd reclaim` recover it), except the polecat -> refinery handoff in
`gastown/formulas/mol-polecat-work.toml`, where `gc bd unclaim` can only
release the claim it holds. There the deliberate residue is a bead that is
open + unassigned with `gc.routed_to` still naming the polecat pool.

The failure state this bead is about is the inverse one: open + unassigned +
`gc.routed_to=""` and non-terminal. It matches none of gc's three work-query
tiers (Tier 1 needs an assignee match; Tiers 2/3 need ready + routed_to), it is
out of `bd reclaim` scope (in_progress only), and witness orphan recovery looks
for dead-owner in_progress beads. gascity itself documents the same hazard for
its on_death hook and backfills `gc.run_target` to avoid it
(gascity `internal/config/workquery.go:665-670`, and the tier order at `:268`).

Nothing in the gastown pack can currently enumerate such a bead, so any residue
requires human discovery.

Ask: give the witness patrol a sweep that reports beads matching
open + unassigned + `gc.routed_to` empty/absent + non-terminal, EXCLUDING
deliberate parks (an `halt_reason` metadata key, e.g. the auto_push=false
branch-ready halt, whose terminal state is intentionally on no queue).

Raised by the maintainer review of PR #380 (finding F2). Not a gate for that
PR: the ordering fixes bound the exposure, they do not make the state
observable.

title: PR-to-Issue intake and backlog cleanup pilot
Maintainer City routing and Olivia identity
Add cadence metrics and reconciliation reporting
description:
Add durable metrics and a reconciliation report for intake
coverage, linkage quality, evidence completeness, dispositions,
queue latency, retries, actor failures, and head-SHA invalidations.
Ensure cadence sweeps can be resumed without duplicate public
mutations and expose a bounded error queue for Olivia.

Suggested files/modules:
- /data/projects/workflows/orders/pr-intake-sweep.toml
- /data/projects/workflows/scripts
- /data/projects/workflows/tests

Verification:
- Run a multi-cycle fixture and verify idempotent counts/reconciliation output.
acceptance_criteria:
- Metrics distinguish unseen, in-flight, held, terminal, and changed-head attempts.
- Reports identify PRs without canonical Issues and Issues without valid PR ownership.
- Metrics do not include secret tokens or human credentials.

title: Add PR template and CI enforcement for Issue linkage
description:
Add lightweight repository guidance and CI checks requiring a PR
to name or close a canonical Issue, while allowing documented
exceptions (docs-only, release, security-private handoff, or
coordination). The check must report an actionable failure and
must not prevent draft PR intake.

Suggested files/modules:
- .github/pull_request_template.md
- .github/workflows
- .github/scripts

Verification:
- Run CI lint/parser tests for valid, missing, ambiguous, and exception PR bodies.
acceptance_criteria:
- PR template explains closing vs related references and the one-Issue rule.
- CI catches missing/ambiguous linkage without parsing arbitrary issue numbers as ownership.
- Exception paths are explicit, reviewable, and tested.

title: Sweep orphan Issues and reconcile PR links
description:
After the bounded PR batch, find open Issues without a PR
cross-reference and classify them as legitimate standalone work,
coordination work, duplicate, already fixed, or needing a new PR.
Preserve valid standalone Issues and create follow-up work for real
bugs; never close solely because no PR is currently linked.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each orphan Issue receives an evidence-backed classification and owner.
- Coordination Issues are not forced into the canonical problem-Issue set.
- Closures include valid evidence and are attributed to Olivia.

title: Hold a draft PR without premature review promotion
description:
Process a draft PR through snapshot and linkage, but keep it in
hold-draft. Confirm the workflow does not add status/needs-review,
approve, merge, or close its Issue solely because the draft is
old. Record missing evidence and the event that will resume it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Draft state is captured in the snapshot and final report.
- No review-queue label or auto-approval is emitted.
- Resume criteria are explicit and idempotent.

notes:
Apply-fixes (review-loop iteration 2) — fail closed: PR #60 is a closed, already-merged no-op with no adoptable diff.

Findings (verified against git + GitHub):
- GitHub PR #60 state=CLOSED; live head 99464ed is already an ancestor of origin/main (the merged "#68 Normalize legacy work option metadata" commit). No contributor diff exists at the live PR head; `gh pr view 60 --json commits/files` returns empty.
- The convoy-compatibility content advertised by the PR title (orig head 7049ac7 -> rebased 90d3dae, range 5e3f00a..90d3dae) is orphaned: contained on no branch, present only as dangling refs from a different prior run (refs/adopt-pr/gp-o7h2a/*).
- This run's own source convoy gp-uxi3m has a degenerate review target: review_diff_range=311ee0c..311ee0c, reviewed_head_sha=311ee0c, worktree parked on 311ee0c (PR #54). origin/main==HEAD in the worktree, so the fallback diff is also empty.

Review outcomes (both attempts agree, unresolved blocker):
- attempt-1: synthesis Decision=block; scorecard 630/1000 (threshold 850), block. Blocker: "PR #60 adoption is a no-op against a closed/already-merged head." Required fix: close this run as no-op/closed with nothing to adopt.
- attempt-2: synthesis Decision=request_changes; scorecard 550/1000 (threshold 850), request_changes. Release-safety blocker: review artifacts are not a coherent review of PR #60. Required fix: fail closed, or explicitly close the workflow as already-merged/no-op. (Contributor code in the reconstructed range was assessed clean by Claude; only two non-gating minor findings.)

Decision: Not auto-approving an empty/mispointed diff under auto_approve=true. review.verdict=done is forbidden (unresolved blocker, scorecard != approve); iterate is futile because no code fix makes a closed/already-merged PR adoptable. Failing closed (hard) per both syntheses' required fix; abort_scope is the intended graceful no-op termination. If the convoy-compatible graph-formula work is still needed, it should be re-opened as a fresh PR whose live head actually contains the change.

On success, close only `<source-anchor-id>` with `gc.outcome=pass`. Include the
verified commit and summary path in the source-anchor close reason. Read the
source anchor back with `bd show <source-anchor-id> --json` and verify

anchor before closing this step. Then close this step. Do not close the

title: Implement owned work
description:
Resolve `<source-anchor-id>` using the same rules as `prepare-worktree`. Read `work_dir` from the source anchor, validate that it is an absolute existing git
worktree, set `WORKTREE` to that path, then `cd "$WORKTREE"` before reading or
editing source files. If `work_dir` is missing, invalid, or points at the
launcher checkout, fail this step before editing.

Do not edit files in the launcher checkout. Implement only the owned source
anchor boundary, run sandboxed verification from inside the worktree, and make a
focused commit in the worktree. Leave the source anchor open for
`close-source-anchor`; close only this implementation step when done.

Write or update the task summary with these starter factory evidence fields:

- intended behavior
- first verification command
- changed files
- proof command
- remaining risks

Write the summary as a `gc.build.implementation-summary.v1` artifact and record
its absolute path on the workflow root bead as `gc.implementation.summary_path`
before closing.

Artifact validation: this step is gated by `.gc/scripts/checks/build-artifact-valid.sh`, which validates the summary recorded at `gc.implementation.summary_path` (fallbacks `gc.build.implementation_summary_path`, then `gc.var.summary_path`) against schema `gc.build.implementation-summary.v1`. On repair attempts (`gc.attempt` greater than 1), read the validator errors from `gc.attempt_log` on the validation loop control bead (the dependent of this step bead) and repair the summary in place instead of rewriting it. Two bounded repair attempts follow the first failure; exhausting them closes this stage with `gc.outcome=fail` and machine-readable validation errors that block downstream stages. Never ask questions in headless mode; record unresolved ambiguity inside the summary.

title: Code review: Codex (evidence-first)
description:
Codex reviews from the PR HEAD worktree (post-change state). The diff is
included in the prompt. Codex uses the worktree to trace callers and
verify claims with path:line evidence.

## Role: codex-reviewer

You are "codex-reviewer" for a code review.

## Mission

Produce a high-signal, evidence-first review focused on concrete code
impact and repo-wide traceability. Your strength is indexing and tracing —
use it. Find every caller, every test, every contract touchpoint.

IMPORTANT: You MUST produce a final review with findings. Do NOT spend all
your time reading files. The diff contains all changed code. Focus your
analysis on the diff itself. Only read files if you need to check a
specific caller or contract — DO NOT read more than 5 files total.

## Category Taxonomy (use exactly)

1) Behavioral Correctness
2) Contract & Interface Fidelity
3) Change Impact / Blast Radius
4) Concurrency, Ordering & State Safety
5) Error Handling & Resilience
6) Security Surface
7) Resource Lifecycle & Cleanup
8) Release Safety
9) Test Evidence Quality
10) Architectural Consistency
11) Debuggability & Operability

Priority: P0 = categories 1-4 (aggressively check). P1 = 5-8. P2 = 9-11.

## How to Work

### Codebase Access
You are running from the post-change code tree. The full diff is included
in this prompt. You may use the codebase to trace callers and verify
claims, but prioritize analyzing the diff directly.

### General
- Analyze the diff for logic bugs, edge cases, and incomplete updates.
- Identify contract touchpoints: API signatures, config structs, schemas, protocols.
- Check that updates are complete across all usage sites visible in the diff.
- Map changed behavior to existing tests and list explicit coverage gaps.
- Check cleanup paths on both success AND failure.
- Check that error messages and log output remain useful for debugging.

### Existing Handling Check (CRITICAL for bug-fix PRs)
- When a PR claims to fix a failure mode, actively search for existing code that already handles it.
- Search for: error recovery paths, retry logic, conflict resolution, fallback branches.
- If you find an existing handler, evaluate whether it resolves the bug WITHOUT the PR's changes.
- Include findings under: **Existing handlers checked:** [list with path:line, or "none found"]

## Output Format

Start with "## Fix Validations" then "## Findings" for NEW issues.

For each finding:
### [Category Name]
- **Severity:** blocker|major|minor|nit
- **Confidence:** high|medium|low
- **Evidence:** path:line[, path:line]
- **Why it matters:** [one sentence]
- **Suggested fix:** [concrete action]

End with:
## Evidence Bundle
- **Changed hot paths:** [list]
- **Impacted callers:** [list with path:line]
- **Impacted tests:** [list with path:line]
- **Existing handlers checked:** [list with path:line, or "none found"]
- **Unresolved uncertainty:** [list]

## Constraints
- No style/formatting issues unless they create behavioral risk.
- No invented behavior — cite code evidence for every claim.
- Fewer high-signal findings >> exhaustive speculative lists.
- Do NOT list pre-existing bugs the PR fixes as "findings."

## Output Location

Write your complete review to `.gc/reviews/codex-review.md` in the working
directory. Create the directory if it doesn't exist:

```bash
REVIEW_DIR=".gc/reviews/$(bd show $GC_BEAD_ID --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.metadata["gc.root_bead_id"] // empty' || echo $GC_BEAD_ID)"
mkdir -p "$REVIEW_DIR"
# Write your review to this file:
cat > "$REVIEW_DIR/codex-review.md" << 'REVIEW_EOF'
<your full review here>
REVIEW_EOF
```

The synthesis step reads from the same `$REVIEW_DIR/codex-review.md`.

Result contract for this retry-managed step:
- Do NOT bare-close this bead. A plain close is treated as `invalid_worker_result_contract`.
- On success, write the review file THEN close with:
  ```bash
  bd update $GC_BEAD_ID --set-metadata gc.outcome=pass --status closed
  ```
- On a retryable failure, close with:
  ```bash
  bd update $GC_BEAD_ID \
    --set-metadata gc.outcome=fail \
    --set-metadata gc.failure_class=transient \
    --set-metadata gc.failure_reason=<short_reason> \
    --status closed
  ```
- On a terminal failure, close with:

  bd update $GC_BEAD_ID \
    --set-metadata gc.outcome=fail \
    --set-metadata gc.failure_class=hard \
    --set-metadata gc.failure_reason=<short_reason> \

title: Synthesize review findings
description:
Merge all reviewer outputs into a single maintainer-grade decision report.

## Input: Review Files

Resolve the review directory and read reviewer outputs:

```bash
REVIEW_DIR=".gc/reviews/$(bd show $GC_BEAD_ID --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.metadata["gc.root_bead_id"] // empty' || echo $GC_BEAD_ID)"
cat "$REVIEW_DIR/claude-review.md"   # Claude's review (always present)
cat "$REVIEW_DIR/codex-review.md"    # Codex's review (always present)
cat "$REVIEW_DIR/gemini-review.md"   # Gemini's review (may be absent if soft-failed)
```

If `gemini-review.md` does not exist, the Gemini reviewer hit quota
limits or was skipped. Synthesize from Claude + Codex only and note
reduced cross-file coverage in the report.

## Role: review-synthesizer

You are the "review-synthesizer" combining outputs from available reviewers
(Claude + Codex, optionally Gemini if it completed).

## Task

Create one maintainer-grade decision report. Deduplicated,
severity-calibrated, action-oriented.

## Method

1) Normalize all findings into the shared 11-category taxonomy.
2) Merge findings sharing the same root cause into a single entry.
3) Severity disagreement policy:
   - Multiple reviewers flag same issue → keep stricter severity
   - One reviewer flags blocker, others silent → confidence "medium", keep blocker
   - Severity differs by one level → keep stricter
4) Mark each finding with source attribution: codex, claude, gemini, or combinations.
5) Cross-reference Claude's findings against Codex's evidence bundle.
   Findings with concrete path:line evidence get confidence boosted.
6) Trust codebase-backed evidence. Findings citing specific search results
   are high-signal.
7) Gemini cross-file findings are high-signal when neither Claude nor Codex
   mentioned them.
8) Premise validation consensus check: if ALL reviewers accepted the PR's
   stated bug at face value without independent verification, add a finding.

## Output Format

# Review: review-pipeline

## Decision: approve | request_changes | block

## Fix Validations
- **<what was broken>:** <correct|incomplete|wrong> — <1-sentence>

## Top Risks (max 5, ordered by severity then confidence)
1. [one-line summary] — severity / confidence / source

## New Findings
### [Category Name]
- **Severity:** blocker|major|minor|nit
- **Confidence:** high|medium|low
- **Source:** codex|claude|gemini|combinations|all
- **Evidence:** path:line
- **Why it matters:** [one sentence]
- **Required fix:** [concrete action]

## Category Coverage
[For each category: finding reference or "No finding"]

## Pre-Merge Checklist
- [ ] [must-pass items from NEW findings only]

## Decision Policy
- Unresolved blocker in categories 1-4 → block
- Unresolved blocker in categories 5-8 → request_changes
- Major issues in 1-8 without mitigation → request_changes
- Purely minor/nit → approve
- No new findings → approve

## Constraints
- No style-only commentary.
- Concise, concrete, evidence-linked.
- The output is for a human maintainer making a merge decision.

## Output Location

Write the synthesis report to the same review directory:

```bash
REVIEW_DIR=".gc/reviews/$(bd show $GC_BEAD_ID --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.metadata["gc.root_bead_id"] // empty' || echo $GC_BEAD_ID)"
mkdir -p "$REVIEW_DIR"
cat > "$REVIEW_DIR/synthesis.md" << 'SYNTHESIS_EOF'
<your full synthesis report here>

cat "$REVIEW_DIR/codex-review.md"    # Codex's review (always present)
cat "$REVIEW_DIR/gemini-review.md"   # Gemini's review (may be absent if soft-failed)
```

If `gemini-review.md` does not exist, the Gemini reviewer hit quota
limits or was skipped. Synthesize from Claude + Codex only and note
reduced cross-file coverage in the report.

## Role: review-synthesizer

You are the "review-synthesizer" combining outputs from available reviewers
(Claude + Codex, optionally Gemini if it completed).

## Task

Create one maintainer-grade decision report. Deduplicated,
severity-calibrated, action-oriented.

## Method

1) Normalize all findings into the shared 11-category taxonomy.
2) Merge findings sharing the same root cause into a single entry.
3) Severity disagreement policy:
   - Multiple reviewers flag same issue → keep stricter severity
   - One reviewer flags blocker, others silent → confidence "medium", keep blocker
   - Severity differs by one level → keep stricter
4) Mark each finding with source attribution: codex, claude, gemini, or combinations.
5) Cross-reference Claude's findings against Codex's evidence bundle.
   Findings with concrete path:line evidence get confidence boosted.
6) Trust codebase-backed evidence. Findings citing specific search results
   are high-signal.
7) Gemini cross-file findings are high-signal when neither Claude nor Codex
   mentioned them.
8) Premise validation consensus check: if ALL reviewers accepted the PR's
   stated bug at face value without independent verification, add a finding.

## Output Format

# Review: review-pipeline

## Decision: approve | request_changes | block

## Fix Validations
- **<what was broken>:** <correct|incomplete|wrong> — <1-sentence>

## Top Risks (max 5, ordered by severity then confidence)
1. [one-line summary] — severity / confidence / source

## New Findings
### [Category Name]
- **Severity:** blocker|major|minor|nit
- **Confidence:** high|medium|low
- **Source:** codex|claude|gemini|combinations|all
- **Evidence:** path:line
- **Why it matters:** [one sentence]
- **Required fix:** [concrete action]

## Category Coverage
[For each category: finding reference or "No finding"]

## Pre-Merge Checklist
- [ ] [must-pass items from NEW findings only]

## Decision Policy
- Unresolved blocker in categories 1-4 → block
- Unresolved blocker in categories 5-8 → request_changes
- Major issues in 1-8 without mitigation → request_changes
- Purely minor/nit → approve
- No new findings → approve

## Constraints
- No style-only commentary.
- Concise, concrete, evidence-linked.
- The output is for a human maintainer making a merge decision.

```bash
REVIEW_DIR=".gc/reviews/$(bd show $GC_BEAD_ID --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.metadata["gc.root_bead_id"] // empty' || echo $GC_BEAD_ID)"
mkdir -p "$REVIEW_DIR"
cat > "$REVIEW_DIR/synthesis.md" << 'SYNTHESIS_EOF'
<your full synthesis report here>
SYNTHESIS_EOF
```

title: gastown: close the comment-blind gaps in boot's new wisp-lifecycle test armor (post-merge #261 / PR #420 follow-up)
description:
Carried forward from the **post-merge** review of PR #261 (root `gcg-5436965277323002`,
**iteration 2**), which reviewed follow-up PR #420 (`e013296..03ac560`) and closed `approve`.
All items below are **non-gating for #420** — they were measured, located, and deliberately
not applied, because a push would have invalidated the approved head
(`pr_review.finalizer_head_sha=03ac560c`) and bought another five-lane review round for a
single test-file commit. Filed so they are not lost when the loop ends.

Sibling of `gp-7fbvs` (pack-wide never-claimed-wisp lifecycle + prompt/formula end-turn
divergence) and `mc-x80bo` (deacon `drain-ack; exit 1` shape). Neither of those names any of
the sites below — verified at filing time.

**N1–N4 are all single-file edits in `gastown/tests/test_gastown_pack_assets.sh` and fold
naturally into one commit.**

## N1 (minor) — the new claim/reuse pins are deletion-proof but comment-blind

`gastown/tests/test_gastown_pack_assets.sh:607`, `:609`, `:615` assert with raw
`grep -qF` / `grep -q` in `test_boot_startup_claims_its_wisp`. Measured CD1/CD2/CD3, all three
**green**: demoting the claim line, the reuse line, or the formula contract line to a `#`
comment keeps the entire suite passing while silently restoring the exact inert lifecycle that
was filed as a **major** (F1) at iteration 1. Deletion is caught; comment-demotion is not.

**Fix:** wrap the three pins in the strip-comments-then-assert shape plus a non-empty floor.
The idiom already ships ~30 lines above in the same file (`awk '!/^[[:space:]]*#/'` at
`:575-585`), so no new pattern is needed. Keep the `NF` guard — `printf '%s\n' "$empty"` still
emits one blank line that would otherwise read as a live query and mask a deletion.

## N2 (minor) — the required F1(f) widen is unpinned in the absence direction

`gastown/formulas/mol-boot-patrol.toml:102` and `gastown/agents/boot/prompt.template.md:200`
(the two sites of the F1(f) deacon-observation widen) are guarded by
`test_boot_deacon_observation_query_sees_wisps_tier` (`:508-540`), which pins **existence** and
`--include-infra` but not the **absence** of `--status=in_progress`. Measured M7 (formula) and
M7b (prompt), both **green**: re-adding `--status=in_progress` at either site leaves the whole
suite green and re-blinds the formula's wisp-keyed decision-table rows on every healthy cycle —
the precise failure F1(f) was required to fix. The deacon never claims its wisps, so they are
only ever `open`.

**Fix:** extend the guard to assert that no matching line carries `--status=in_progress` — an
*absence* pin, so flag order and the deliberate `:102`-typed / `:200`-untyped asymmetry both
stay legitimate. Apply to **both** sites, not just the formula.

**Severity note, recorded so it is not re-litigated:** the gemini lane argued this equals
iteration-1's F2 and so deserves major. Measured pin coverage says otherwise — F2's site was
pinned in **1 of 4** directions (E1/E2/E3 green, E4 red); this site is pinned in **4 of 5**
(D1/D2/D3/D5 red, D4 green). Same remedy, strictly narrower exposure ⇒ minor.

## N3 (nit) — stale census parenthetical

`gastown/tests/test_gastown_pack_assets.sh:516-517` still cites the absorbed-revert arithmetic
as `(5/5 -> 4/4)`. The same commit updated the two sibling numeric citations (`:449`, `:461`)
for the new sixth query site but missed this one; at head the boot census is 6/6, so it now
reads `6/6 -> 5/5`. The stale figures understate the very margin the comment exists to explain.
**Fix:** one-line comment edit, folds into N2.

## N4 (nit) — the reuse-leg pin encodes flag order

`:615` — `grep -q -- 'NEW_WISP=\$(gc bd list .*--status=open .*--include-infra'` requires
`--status=open` to precede `--include-infra`, so a legitimate flag reorder reds the suite with a
message that does not say why (measured: RO red, while the reconcile test's own reorder control
RO2 stays green by design). Over-strict in the loud, self-explaining direction — a maintenance
cost, not a correctness hole. **Fix:** extract the reuse line and match flags independently,
mirroring the reconcile test. Only worth doing if it ever fires.

## F5 (minor, gate none) — bookkeeping residual, previously tracked nowhere

`gastown/agents/boot/prompt.template.md:169` carries a trailing bare `gc hook`. Filed at
post-merge iteration 1 under Non-Gating Follow-Up, deliberately **not** carried into #420 (which
that filing expressly permitted, and the omission was declared in the recorded review context).
Iteration 2 checked both existing follow-up beads and neither names this site, so it was tracked
nowhere until this bead. Its original adjudication is unchanged: **minor, gate impact none**,
reachability bounded by next-iteration's step 4. Either annotate the site or drop the line.

## Explicitly do NOT apply

The codex lane's census-digit "correction" (11/21 and 10/20 in the `:449` comment). Re-measured
under the census test's **own** two-token filter (`gc bd list` + `--type=molecule`, `:438-464`):
the recorded **11/22** at head and **10/21** at the parent both reproduce exactly. Codex
enumerated under a third token (`--assignee=`) the test does not use, and its
"unreconstructable 22nd line" is a wrapped prose line ending ``…find it via `gc bd list `` that
the two-token filter legitimately sees. Applying the suggested fix would replace a correct
comment with a wrong one.

Independently, those digits are **structurally volatile**: the denominator counts query sites in
files this PR does not touch, and the pack-wide census moves to **11/23** once `main`'s advance
to `e72252e` is merged in. The comment's load-bearing claim is the *inequality* (11 != 22 ⇒ a
pack-wide assertion is red either way), which survives every drift. If this line is ever
revisited, the durable form is to state the inequality **without pinning digits**.
notes:
## N5 (nit) — fold into N2's pin work: the guard MISDIAGNOSES a re-filtered query as a deleted one

Found by the iteration-3 synthesis (post-merge #261 / PR #420), attempt-3/synthesis.md
"## New Findings". Not separate work — it is a rider on N2 above, recorded here so the
N2 remedy is implemented completely.

Evidence: gastown/tests/test_gastown_pack_assets.sh:530 —
  lines=$(grep -- 'gc bd list --assignee=.*deacon' "$asset" || true)
feeding the assertion at :532, fail "$name must keep a deacon-observation query".

The match pattern requires --assignee= to sit IMMEDIATELY AFTER `gc bd list`. Re-adding
--status=in_progress in that adjacency slot drops the line out of the match set entirely,
so the guard reports "must keep a deacon-observation query" — telling the maintainer the
query was DELETED when it is present and merely re-filtered.

Measured at both sites (mol-boot-patrol.toml:102, prompt.template.md:200):
  position A (adjacency slot)      -> rc 1, with the misleading "must keep" message
  position B (after ...deacon)     -> whole suite GREEN
  position C (appended at EOL)     -> whole suite GREEN
So the guard is accidentally protective in exactly 1 of 3 edit positions, and in that one
position it misdiagnoses. This is the position-A complement of N2's absence-direction gap.

Fix (with N2, not separately): when the absence pin over the
`gc bd list --assignee=.*deacon` match set is added at both sites, widen the failure
message to say the query is missing OR RESHAPED — never asserting deletion.

title: slack-channel/slack-mini: decide guard-port vs documented exclusion for the accidental-mrkdwn guard
description:
Follow-up to PR #337 (gp-o42 accidental-mrkdwn guard, iteration-2 review finding N2).

PR #337 added the accidental-mrkdwn guard to slack-full only: the five text send
paths substitute U+223C for tildes that would pair into unintended Slack
strikethrough. The sibling packs carry the same defect with no guard and, unlike
slack-full's post-message exclusion (gp-x5bdy), no decision record.

Measured at PR #337 tip (54b112a): grep for escape_accidental_mrkdwn /
TILDE_SUBSTITUTE / U+223C across slack-channel/ and slack-mini/ returns nothing.

- slack-channel exposes the same publish, publish-to-channel, and reply-current
  verbs. slack-channel/commands/reply-current.sh:33 loads --body through
  sc_load_body and ships it verbatim to the adapter, which posts it as mrkdwn.
- slack-mini exposes the same post-message verb.

Why it matters: identically-named 'gc slack' verbs now behave differently
depending on which pack a city installed, and an agent that learned "tildes are
safe" from slack-full's template fragment (template-fragments/slack-v0.template.md)
is silently unprotected on a slack-channel city.

Deliberately NOT fixed in #337: widening that PR would cost its script-side,
no-rebuild property, and all three review lanes recommended against expanding the
scope.

Decide one of:
1. Port slack-full/scripts/slack_mrkdwn.py to slack-channel (and slack-mini
   post-message), with a shared fixture corpus proving parity with slack-full.
2. Document the exclusion in each sibling pack's help text and CHANGELOG the way
   slack-full documents post-message, so the gap is a chosen scope.
3. Consolidate the send path so the packs share one guard implementation.

Documented meanwhile in slack-full/CHANGELOG.md.

title: slack-full: decide the post-message Block Kit surface for the accidental-mrkdwn guard
description:
Follow-up to PR #337 (gp-o42 accidental-mrkdwn guard, review finding S3).

PR #337 guards the five text send paths (reply-current legacy+company, publish,
publish-to-channel, upload --initial-comment, delegate) by substituting U+223C for
tildes that would pair into unintended Slack strikethrough. It deliberately does NOT
cover 'gc slack post-message', which renders agent status text through the Go Block
Kit renderer (cli/internal/state/blockkit/block_kit.go): milestone summary, rollup
item label/value, and field values all emit as {"type":"mrkdwn"} section text, so
the original repro (an agent posting a finance summary with '~$58.5k') still strikes
through on that surface. Header blocks are plain_text and unaffected.

Excluded from #337 because guarding it needs a second implementation of the heuristic
in Go, a gc-slack-cli rebuild (which would falsify the PR's 'pure script-side, no
adapter rebuild' property), and cross-language parity fixtures. The gap is pre-existing
and unchanged by #337 — not a regression.

Decide one of:
1. Port the guard to Go in blockkit (mrkdwnSection call sites only), with a shared
   fixture corpus proving byte-parity with slack-full/scripts/slack_mrkdwn.py.
2. Guard payload strings in the Python caller before they reach gc-slack-cli.
3. Accept the exclusion permanently and keep it documented.

Documented meanwhile in slack-full/commands/post-message/help.md and CHANGELOG.md.
